item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Sun Nov 8, 7:00 PM
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Tech Talks — Thu Nov 12, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: TBD
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Parent Workshop: Learning to Read, Let's talk about Decoding (adults only) — Thu Nov 12, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Storytime Room
item.description:
The Library’s Reading Specialist will be hosting her first parent workshop of the 2026-2027 school year. This will be the first of 3 workshops in a series about Literacy. Parents, caregivers and reading tutors will learn about the Science of Reading and the process of learning how to read. We will also discuss how to support your child’s literacy learning at home. Lastly, participants will learn about the resources available to check out of the library and how to use them at home. Registration required.
This is a hybrid event. You will receive the link after registering.
(The 2nd workshop about Reading Comprehension will take place in December. The 3rd workshop of the series about Writing will take place in January.)
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Theme of the Month Book Club — Thu Nov 12, 6:30 PM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
Looking for new books to discover and fellow readers to connect with? Join Theme of the Month Book Club, a monthly gathering where participants read a book of their choice based on a shared theme and come together to discuss their selections.
Each month, a new theme will be announced—such as historical fiction, books by debut authors, found family, travel, mysteries, and more! Rather than everyone reading the same title, participants are free to choose any book that fits the theme and share their thoughts with the group.
This relaxed and welcoming book club is a great way to broaden your reading horizons, discover new recommendations, and enjoy lively conversations with other book lovers.
Please register to reserve your spot!
Themes:
September: Fresh Starts
October: Banned Books
November: Gratitude and Gathering
December: Home for the Holidays
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: [MILL Senior Friday] Chair Yoga for Everyone with Pammi — Fri Nov 13, 10:30 AM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Join us on Fridays for a day full of events for Seniors with the MILL @ MPL! All events are free and open to the public. Registration is recommended unless otherwise noted.
With this class there is a focus on basic yoga postures, breathing techniques, meditation and supported standing poses for balance, range of motion and flexibility. Most of the class is done in a chair or the chair can also be used to support balance.
ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR PAMMI ANANDANI is a certified yoga instructor specializing in teaching a chair yoga style called Yoga for Everyone. She has taught yoga to seniors at Riverdale Y, Lennox Hill Neighborhood House and Cedar Grove Seniors among others.
HOW TO REGISTER This class is run by the MILL. Please register for classes directly through their website here.
For questions about MILL classes please call 973-744-3278.
MILL @ MPL is made possible through a partnership between the MILL, Montclair Public Library and Partners for Health.

item.title: [MILL Senior Friday] World of Film with Mark Phelan — Fri Nov 13, 1:30 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Join us on Fridays for a day full of events for Seniors with the MILL @ MPL! All events are free and open to the public. Registration is recommended unless otherwise noted.
The White Ribbon (2009) | R
Using their social status and harsh punishments, a baron, a doctor and a pastor rule over a small German village. One day, the doctor falls off his horse after it trips over a wire strung between two trees. More pranks follow, seemingly without reason, all directed at the village's upper class and growing increasingly more brutal with time. There are no suspects, but a local schoolteacher has his suspicions.
ABOUT THE INSTRUCTOR MARK PHELAN - I am a lifelong film fanatic who eats, breathes, sleeps and drinks movies. I have studied with Donald Spoto at the New School in NYC and have a BA and MA in Speech and Theatre from MSU. item.title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays) — Sun Nov 15, 9:00 AM
item.description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.
⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).
**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one

item.description: A Most Beautiful Thing (2020, 1h35) follows the story of the first African American public high school rowing team in the United States. Formed in the 1990s at Manley High School and based in Chicago’s West Side, the team was made up of young men, many of whom were members of rival gangs. Reuniting after 20 years, the team gets back on the water to prepare to race in the 2019 Chicago Sprints, the largest rowing regatta in the Midwest. In the process, Arshay Cooper, the team’s captain, takes inspiration from the past and reaches out to the Chicago Police Department to show that rowing can bring even people with the most disparate of backgrounds together. item.title: 🚶Yanticaw Park Nutley — Sat Nov 7, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! Meet along Park Drive in Nutley near the Orechio Sports Complex. We'll walk about 3.5 mile through scenic Yanticaw Park, up to Kingsland St. and back. The path is paved and mostly flat.
Please check the event page beforehand in case of any changes. Inclement weather will cancel the walk.
The Yanticaw Park is an Essex County-owned park in Nutley, New Jersey. It is located between Centre Street and Chestnut Street, extending west to Passaic Avenue.
Essex County began purchasing land in 1911 for creation of the park. Wetlands in the park were drained, and a dam was set up to form a lake. The park was completed in 1914. In 1962, the lake, containing a small island was drained and a channel was dug as a continuation of the natural third river from the south.
